plan: In a first-price sealed-bid auction with rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly less than your private value to maximize profit while still having a chance to win. Given my value of $26, I'll bid slightly below it to ensure a positive profit margin if I win. I'll bid $25 to balance winning probability and profit maximization.

Given my private value of $18, I should bid slightly less than my value to maximize profit. Bidding exactly my value risks a zero profit if I win. A bid of $17.9 balances winning chances and potential profit, as rational bidders would bid close to their values. This bid assumes others bid rationally and close to their values too, potentially between $0 and $49.

Given my value of $21, I should bid slightly below my value to maximize expected profit while minimizing the risk of losing. Since all bidders are rational, they will bid close to their value. A bid of $20.9 balances winning chances and profit, ensuring I don't overpay if I win.
